**Finding submitted: `missing` (critical rule IP), confidence 0.85.**

**What I found.** The Agreement is silent on intellectual property ownership. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site at its own cost (§§ 1.1–1.3), the Company supplies all Content (§ 2.1), and HDI holds the Company's "Content, user information, data" (§ 8.1) — but no provision says who owns the Site, the deliverables the Company pays for through Net Sales, the Content, or the customer data collected through the Site. There is also no licence back of any HDI platform IP embedded in the Site.

The nearest analogues are not ownership clauses:
- § 5.2 — exclusive artistic/editorial control and approval rights (control, not title)
- § 5.3 — merchant of record and title to the *products*, not IP
- § 6.1 — a narrow "Deerskin" Marks licence to HDI with no implied licences (helpful, and preserved)
- § 8 — confidentiality (use restrictions, not ownership)
- § 10.2 — disclaims co-ownership/joint venture

**Direction check.** Nothing assigns Company IP or data to HDI, and no joint ownership is created, so this is a genuine gap rather than walk-away territory — which is why the redline adds protection rather than reversing an adverse assignment.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** New § 5.5 inserted after p0035, at the preferred position: Company ownership of the Site, deliverables and customer data with an express HDI assignment; HDI retains its pre-existing software, systems, tools and know-how; and a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to any HDI materials embedded in the Site, with a no-joint-ownership / no-assignment-to-HDI backstop.

One point worth flagging for the negotiation: because HDI bears all build and hosting costs and holds a two-year post-term non-compete (§ 6.3), HDI may push back on full assignment of the Site itself. The fallback — HDI owning its generic tools and platform while we take a perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable licence to the Site deliverables plus outright ownership of Content and customer data — would still be compliant, and customer data ownership should be treated as non-negotiable in that trade.
